caption:
This is the inside-out version of W. Edwards Deming’s observation: “A bad system will beat a good person every time.”

Where do you see yourself in this story?

Do you hear yourself as a child being told to “be a good person”?

As an adult do you still hear this echoing in your head when you see someone choosing to take care of themselves before they take care of the system?

If the “good person” stands between us and understanding the full cost of our relational models, why is this “good”?

And if Deming is correct and a bad system beats a good person every time, why does the good person persist?
question: Can being “good” become “bad” if it keeps harmful systems alive? Where do we draw the line?
